verdict.line: You lose if you grind out slow auto-trades that feed his Darkness Rise aura and get isolated by his R; you win if you collapse trades into one empowered burst that destroys his W shield before he can heal off it.

brief.thesis: Both champions gate their power behind a threshold mechanic — your Fury above 50 empowers all three abilities, his passive Darkness Rise needs 3 landed hits to grant a damage aura and move speed. The 49.6% win rate over 2622 games reflects that most players trade the wrong way: extended auto-trading feeds his aura for free, while a single burst (Q-W-E in one window) denies it and, if timed against his W (Indestructible), destroys the shield he's trying to stack before he can consume it to heal. Win this lane by forcing single decisive exchanges, not a drawn-out poke war.

theirWindow.when: Darkness Rise active and his E up
theirWindow.what: His passive grants a damage aura and move speed after 3 landed hits on champions or monsters, and E (Death's Grasp, range 700) pulls all enemies in an area to him. If both are live, disengage rather than keep trading — you'll eat aura damage and risk being pulled into his minion wave for a follow-up Obliterate.

yourWindow.when: Fury above 50 and he activates W
yourWindow.what: Dash in with E (Slice and Dice) then land your empowered W (Ruthless Predator) — at over 50 Fury it hits three times, destroys damage shields on the target, and stuns for 1.5 seconds. Timed against his W (Indestructible), it erases the shield he's storing before he can consume it to heal, and because it's one burst rather than three separate hits, it denies a Darkness Rise proc too.

start.why: Sustains you through early trades and adds the flat AD that makes empowered Q and W hit harder once Fury builds.

boots.why: His entire kit is magic damage (Q, passive aura, E, R), so flat magic resist directly shrinks every poke and all-in he throws at you.

core.why: The shield and execute proc reward a clean, single all-in window — exactly the burst pattern that punishes his W shield instead of feeding his passive.
Stacking armor shred from autos and empowered E amplifies your physical burst enough to keep outpacing his Indestructible sustain.
Bleed-based healing lets you survive the magic damage trade and keep resetting Fury through autos after the fight.

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacking adaptive force into healing at max stacks is built for extended all-ins and directly offsets the sustain he gets from consuming his W shield.

summoners.why: Ignite's grievous wounds cuts the healing he gets from consuming his W shield, so commit all-ins once it's up and his sustain is weakest.

playing.title: Punish his W shield
playing.detail: When he activates W (Indestructible) to start storing damage, dash in with E and land empowered W if Fury is above 50 — the triple slash destroys his stored shield before he can consume it to heal.

playing.title: Single-burst, don't auto-trade
playing.detail: Favor landing full ability combos over prolonged auto-attacking; Darkness Rise only needs 3 landed hits to proc his damage aura and move speed, so spacing out pokes feeds it for free.

playing.title: Track his Obliterate cooldown
playing.detail: Q (Obliterate, range 675) hits hardest on a single target and ramps to a 4s cooldown at rank 5 — once it's down, step into range for your own trade since he has no poke to punish you with.

playing.title: Respect Death's Grasp near minions
playing.detail: E (range 700) pulls all enemies in an area to him — don't stand near the wave within that range from level 3 onward, since getting pulled into minions sets up a free follow-up Obliterate.

playing.title: Save E for the confirmed all-in
playing.detail: Slice and Dice is both your gap closer and, past 50 Fury, an armor-shredding empowered dash — hold it for stun-confirmed all-ins at levels 3-5 rather than spending it just to farm Fury.

playing.title: Ignite before you commit
playing.detail: Confirm Ignite is off cooldown before all-inning past level 6 — it denies the heal he gets from popping his W shield and can outright deny a kill reset.

playing.title: Don't overextend once his R is up
playing.detail: From level 6, Realm of Death (range 650) drags you into an isolated fight and steals a portion of your stats if he kills you — avoid being caught alone past mid lane even though solo-kill rate is measured even.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and win rates above come from measured OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning — Fury thresholds, the W-shield interaction, and the Darkness Rise proc condition — is my own tactical read, not measured data.
